title: [Bug] GPU extension
body:
##### System information (version)
- OpenVINO Source => Runtime
- OpenVINO Version => Version 2023.0 
- Operating System / Platform => Windows 64 Bit
- Compiler => Visual Studio 2019 / Cmake
- Problem classification:  model load with GPU extension 
- Device use:  GPU 
- Framework: onnx

##### Detailed description
<!-- your description -->
With OpenVino 2022.2,  I have implemented a GPU customization layer, the code like this:
`core.set_property("GPU", { { CONFIG_KEY(CONFIG_FILE), xmlPath } });
core.add_extension(vinoParam.customLibPath);`

It work correctly.

But when I update OpenVino to 2023.0, it can not read_model successfuly which can not recognizethe custom layer.
About the GPU customization layer, do I need to make any changes or upgrades after upgrade to 2023.0?

comments.author: participant3
comments.body:
@reporter Could you check if the model has set domain?
You can achieve it via:
```
import onnx
model = onnx.load("your_model.onnx")
print(model.opset_import)
```
If the domain is not empty, could you try replace:
```
core.add_extension(ov::frontend::OpExtension<CustomHough>());
```
with:
```
#include "openvino/frontend/onnx/extension/op.hpp"
...
core.add_extension(ov::frontend::onnx::OpExtension<CustomHough>("CustomHough", "TheModelDomain"));
```
where `TheModelDomain` is from `opset_import`.

comments.author: participant3
comments.body:
@reporter Thank you for the test. It looks like the domain of the model is empty (`15` is probably opset version in your case). The output of `opset_import` can look like:
```
[domain: ""
version: 13
, domain: "ai.onnx.ml"
version: 2
]
```
Let's go to the next step. A single node can have set custom domain even if model's domain is empty.
Could you check:
```
import onnx

model = onnx.load('your_model.onnx')
for node in model.graph.node:
    if node.op_type == "CustomHough":
        print(node.domain)
        break
``` 
Note the the result can be empty also here (if empty, the reason of bug is other than I've thought).

comments.author: participant5
comments.body:
@reporter The default inference precision of the GPU plugin is `f16` now.
So, if your custom opencl kernel uses `float` type, the inference precision should be set as `f32`.
Could you test your app again with the below config?

`core.set_property(ov::hint::inference_precision(ov::element::f32));`
